claims.claim: X-Kid is a Green Day trilogy single that reached three Billboard charts.
claims.assessment: Article gives the chart table and places the song on Tre, the third album of the trilogy. The title avoids the contested single ordinal, because the album article lists one single while the song article calls it the second.

claims.claim: X-Kid made three Billboard lists in 2013.
claims.assessment: Chart table is headed 2013 and lists three entries.
Chart table: Canada Rock, Billboard, 38.

claims.claim: US Hot Rock and Alternative Songs peaked at 48.
claims.assessment: Chart table: US Hot Rock & Alternative Songs, Billboard, 48. The ampersand is written as "and" in copy.

claims.claim: US Rock and Alternative Airplay peaked at 36.
claims.assessment: Chart table: US Rock & Alternative Airplay, Billboard, 36.

claims.claim: The A.V. Club heard the opening as a blend of Who Wrote Holden Caulfield? and One Of My Lies, both from Kerplunk.
claims.assessment: Jason Heller's review, quoted in the song article, describes a rousing intro that becomes a hybrid of those two songs. Kerplunk is the band's second album per the same article.

claims.claim: This upload is the ordinary long form rather than the play-along, with the bass part and the note highway in frame.
claims.assessment: Distinguishes 0027 from 0008, which is the dedicated play-along. Description of the visible overlay only.

claims.claim: Ask for a Green Day song on Kick, the chat mirrors on Twitch while it runs, and trilogy debates go to Discord.
claims.source: Standing channel practice in existing copy
claims.assessment: House order and one URL each. No stream schedule asserted.

claims.claim: Quiz: X-Kid peaked at 36 on which Billboard chart? Options Canada Rock, Hot Rock and Alternative Songs, Rock and Alternative Airplay.
claims.assessment: Answer C, Rock and Alternative Airplay, per the chart table. The description states all three figures, so the question is deliberately answerable from the copy.

claims.claim: Artist-wide genres are punk rock, pop punk, alternative rock, skate punk and power pop, and this normal long form takes the five long-form genre lists plus Long Form All Genres.
claims.assessment: Artist-level classification used for the whole catalogue, not a claim that this recording sits in every genre. Routing follows the standing rule for normal long forms.

distinct_fact_and_source: The 2013 Billboard chart run across three lists, plus the A.V. Club reading of the intro against two Kerplunk songs. Different from 0008, which uses the cassette video and the Jingletown studio facts, and from the Shorts. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Kid ; https://www.avclub.com/green-day-tre-1798175239
uniqueness_assessment: Zero five-word phrases shared with the copy corpus and zero with the other four X-Kid packages. The chart numbers and the Kerplunk comparison appear only in this package. The gate report returns zero cross-video signals.
uncertainties_and_removed_claims: The song article calls X-Kid the second single from the album while the album article lists it as the only single from Tre, so the copy says trilogy single and does not state an ordinal. The A.V. Club wording is a critical comparison, not a statement about composition. The 93.8% YouTube advertising share in the analytics is recorded in the folder evidence and is not treated as something copy can correct. Current playlist membership and pin state are not asserted. Historical screenshots cannot establish live settings.
